title: One Empty DNS Record Took Down Thousands of Apps (AWS, One Year Later)
topic: AWS us-east-1 outage, Oct 2025 (DNS race condition)
whyCare: 'Big Tech scale' failure stories are the format that wins on tech Shorts; AWS's own post-event summary makes it fully sourceable. One-year anniversary: Oct 19-20.

evidence.claim: AWS post-event summary: a latent race condition in DynamoDB's automated DNS management left an empty DNS record for the us-east-1 regional endpoint (Oct 19-20 2025)
Fireship 'US-EAST-1 is humanity's weakest link...' 1,148,219 views; ByteMonk 'How a Tiny Bug Crashed AWS' 73,639 views (both ~11 months)
tech.md: ByteByteGo's top Shorts are 'Big Tech scale' hooks (1.3M-2.4M views)

competitors.title: How a Tiny Bug Crashed AWS | DynamoDB us-east-1 Outage Explained (ByteMonk)

angle: Diagram: Planner -> two Enactors writing one DNS record; a slow Enactor applies an old plan, cleanup deletes it -> record empty (status). Apps' packets to DynamoDB fail (cross). Lesson card: automation needs guards against stale plans.
hook: October 20th, 2025: one DNS record went empty, and thousands of apps went dark.
strengths: Proven demand; primary source available; strong diagram story
weaknesses: Anniversary passes before the open slots (Oct 25-27), so it reads as a retrospective; must follow AWS's summary exactly, no speculation; 'thousands of apps' needs a cited source on production day
